q: Which correctly summarises the products of ONE turn of the Krebs cycle?
options: 2 CO2, 3 reduced NAD, 1 reduced FAD, 1 ATP
1 CO2, 2 reduced NAD, 2 reduced FAD, 2 ATP
3 CO2, 3 reduced NAD, 1 reduced FAD, 1 ATP
2 CO2, 4 reduced NAD, 0 reduced FAD, 2 ATP
explanation: Acetyl (2C) joins oxaloacetate (4C) to form citrate (6C). Two decarboxylations release 2 CO2 (6C → 5C → 4C), and four oxidations reduce 3 NAD+ and 1 FAD. One ATP is made by substrate-level phosphorylation, and oxaloacetate is regenerated. Per glucose (2 turns): 4 CO2, 6 reduced NAD, 2 reduced FAD and 2 ATP.
